title: Discovering Erroll Garner at Tondelayo's and giving him his first group job
summary: When Tatum went home ill, Stewart hired Garner, whom he found at Tondelayo's on 52nd Street, for the Three Deuces; Garner credited him with his first professional group gig.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Well, Tatum was from what, Toledo?

He was from, originally from Toledo, and, of course, at that time he had a home in -- when we were in New York, he still had a home in L. A., and he wasn't feeling too well, so he had to go home, and that's when I got a hold of
Erroll Garner and couple other players that I mentioned.
Now, how did you discover, how did you discover Garner?

Well, he was working on the Street, doing a single at a place down the street from the Three Deuces called Tondelayo's. And he hadn't been on the Street too long. In fact he hadn't been in New York too long. In the late '30s it was, I think, or was it --
It was in the '40s, wasn't it, the early '40s.
The early '40s.
The early '40s?
The early '40s, that's right.
So you formed a quartet sometime during the period when you were with Tatum.
That's right.
Or while he was there.
That's right. That's for sure.
Uh-huh. Like '43, '44?
Now, did you -- now, he didn't -- Garner didn't read?
No, he didn't read, but he was a beautiful piano player, yes.
So now, did you find at the time he
could, he had the kind of variety of keys that he played in (inaudible)?
Oh, yes, he played quite a few.
So you didn't have any --
(Simultaneous remarks.)
No problems.

Yeah, after Tatum left, fortunately, I was able to get a hold of Garner to play with me at the Three Deuces. And he went up, even till Erroll passed, he gave me credit for giving him his first professional gig, you know, with a group (inaudible), and it worked out so wonderful.
